items.note: T3 says a fixed linear network exchanges two banks and T4 names three-element subsets, but neither gives the eight-row schedule, the gates, the restoration of arbitrary scratch values or the signed map (X,Y)->(-Y,X).
T3 says intermediate frames cancel, but it gives no edge operator D_v D_u^{-1}, no commutation with pointwise gates and no endpoint operator D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}.
Only T4's quote (line 159) alludes to subspaces attached to gates. The step's own claim has no labels, no orthogonality of neighbouring triples, no L=Ich and no budget Wm-2N+2L with L<N/2.
No step mentions the shear (H,D)->(H+D,D), the rational matrices M or the identity endpoint difference. These are the bit procedure's endpoint operator in the paper (lines 150-153).
No step mentions the phase frames C_U, the translation kernels aI+bX_v or the C^{tensor m} endpoint operator of the complex network.

T4 states s<Wm and T5 says it gives a power below 1, which matches lines 167-175. It does not distinguish the two networks' s_b and s_c, gives no source of the inequality (L<N/2) and no tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}.

T1 claims linear cost for 'stream operations, controlled shifts' generically, without the specific digit moves, cyclic row splitting or the controlled update y->y+a(controls) mod q^b with its conditions.
Neither the lower-triangular factorization nor the rank-many interchanges per matrix shear appears anywhere in the plan.

T5 gives the recursive structure (s calls at parameter f on volume V/W, cost per volume a power below 1), which matches lines 170-175. It omits the additive O(1) overhead, the shear-to-interchange completion and the row-divisibility condition.

T6 gives the O(Vu^tau), tau<1 bound for interchanging disjoint u-bit fields correctly. It drops the requirement that the addresses form a complete Cartesian product (line 96; shape [P]x[2^u]x[G]x[2^u]x[B] in the lemma).
No step mentions binary changes of basis P_M, the child calls C^{tensor f} or the recovery of H_0 from C via H_0=bSCS.

Only T1's quote (lines 177-179: whole-chunk moves, controlled shifts, correction of exceptional addresses) alludes to it. The step's own claim concerns elementary linear-time operations, and no XOR of selected bits, bad set or cost appears.

T5's generic recursion covers both procedures, but the layer recurrence's defining content is missing: the node overhead O((eK)^tau+1), the leaves F(e)=O(e) below d^beta, the row index from q_0 chunks, and the resulting lambda'.

T7 states the H_0 layer on the same bit of at most d chunks at cost O(Vd^{lambda'}), lambda'<1, matching lines 102-111. It omits that intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics with a single final truncation Q_p, the error bound, and the parameter conditions (K=floor(d^c), the record length r).

S6 names synthetic transforms whose twiddles are signed shifts, and S6.1 names the retained frequency order. There is no omega_t=y^{2r/t}, no F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I, no bit-reversed order or layout L, and no error or cost.
S6.2 names Kronecker-style signed packing and the O(n log n) multiplier as a subroutine. It gives no evaluation point 2^{4p}, centered residues, reduction mod y^r+1 or cost O(rp log(rp)).

S6.1 says in words that the forward transforms keep a common order through the pointwise product. There is no M_r=(f*g)/(rM), no error bound and no cost. S6 also wrongly calls the convolution exact (see errors).

S3 says resampling expresses each transform through a power-of-two tensor transform with the permutations kept in the identity. It gives no identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, no condition theta>p/alpha^4 and no tensor form or cost.

S4 names Bluestein's identity, which converts the middle transform with its target permutation into convolution, but gives no chirp or formula. The cancellation of the source permutation R (lines 206-208, eq:source-permutation-cancel) appears nowhere in the plan.
Apart from kappa=2^{-182} in S0, no step gives the fixed rational exponents, the sizes b, p, d, K, T, r or the choice of prime source lengths.
S2 says a Chinese-remainder map places the digits on distinct prime cyclic axes and preserves convolution. It gives no map x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, no triangular digit form and no implementation.

S5 describes the twist qualitatively (the negative wrap restores the cyclic wrap after untwisting), which is faithful. It does not give the defining map x_d->zeta y with zeta=e^{pi i/r} or the formula for M_C.

The tree lists the reductions in the paper's order. It never assembles the source transform F=2^gamma B_0 QF_t A=RF_s, the opposite transform by conjugation or the six-step algorithm with its scales by S and 2^{2b+4}S.

S7 states the decisive inequality (coefficient error below 1/2, then rounding and carries give the exact product). It has no error chain, no role for p=6b or gamma<=b/4, and puts rounding before rescaling, whereas the paper scales before rounding.
S0 states the final bound O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) with kappa=2^{-182} correctly, but no step gives the cost table, the margins g_i or why the minimum margin 2^{-181}=2kappa fixes kappa.
S0 only lists 'nlogn-conjecture-history' as a dependency. No step says how the bound negates an eventual c_A n lg n lower bound.

errors.says: Convolution over C[y]/(y^r+1) on the remaining axes is computed exactly and fast.
errors.paper: The ring convolution M_r has only an approximation, with error less than sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p} (Proposition prop:synthetic-convolution). Exactness of the product comes only at the end, from the error bound below 1/2 and rounding.

errors.says: rounding, rescaling and carry propagation give the exact product
errors.paper: The numerators are first multiplied exactly by S and then by 2^{2b+4}S, and only then rounded to integers, followed by Phi^{-1} and carry propagation.

errors.says: Gaussian resampling expresses each Fourier transform of arbitrary axis length through a power-of-two tensor transform
errors.paper: Resampling acts on the source transforms of the chosen distinct prime lengths s_i, coprime to t_i with theta>p/alpha^4, not on arbitrary lengths.

errors.says: A fixed linear network ... exchanges two banks of values, so intermediate frames cancel and a call reduces to smaller calls.
errors.paper: Intermediate frames cancel because a common frame commutes with each pointwise linear gate, not because the network exchanges banks. Edges reduce to smaller calls because of the chosen intermediate labels.

errors.says: Elementary tape operations ... cost linear time (supported by the quote at line 177)
errors.paper: Line 177 concerns changes of numerical address coordinates by whole-chunk moves, controlled shifts and correction of exceptional addresses. It does not support the linear-cost claim, which is in Lemmas lem:elementary-streams and lem:ordered-affine-streams.

chain: The top level follows the paper's reduction order (digits, CRT, resampling, chirp, twist, synthetic convolution, exact recovery), but each step only names its reduction without formulas, and the cancellation of the source permutation is missing. The tape-procedure branch T thins out: it jumps from 'three-element subsets give s<Wm' to the recursive saving with no subspace labels, shear or phase interfaces, matrix shears, phase frames or packed bit addition. The plan has no parameter choice or cost table, so the main bound is asserted rather than reached, and S6 wrongly calls the convolution exact.
